# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 14
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 14

---

*[AFTER THE MARTYRDOM. The story finds its ending.]*

1. They buried Thomas and the believers gathered together — silent, fasting, grief-stricken.

2. In the night, Thomas came to Mygdonia. He appeared to her and said: "Daughter — don't be afraid. I haven't left you. My Lord Jesus Christ — the one I believe in — is with you. He is with all who believe in him."

3. Mygdonia's fear left her. She went and told the others what she had seen.

4. Days passed. And then Misdaeus — the king's own son, the man who had given the order — his child was seized by a demon that tormented the boy terribly.

5. Misdaeus thought about it for a long time. And then he thought: *I could go to that man's tomb. Take some of his bones. Lay them on my son. Maybe he would be healed.*

6. He went. But the bones were gone. One of the believers had taken them — carried them all the way to the West.

7. Misdaeus found only dust where the bones had lain. He took that dust and placed it on his son.

8. His son was healed immediately.

9. Misdaeus believed. He was baptized.

10. "I believe in you, Lord Jesus Christ," he said. "And I am asking you — forgive me for what I did to your servant Thomas."

11. After that, many in India came to believe — men and women, young and old. The mission did not die with the missionary.

12. The churches Thomas had built held firm. They grew. They spread.

13. And all of this has been written down — the miracles, the signs, the whole story of what Thomas did in India — so that those who come after will know, and in knowing, will believe.

14. Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit,
    now and for ever and ever.
    Amen.

---
*PNEUMA note: The final chapter resolves every thread. Thomas's post-mortem appearance to Mygdonia confirms that death has not ended his presence among his people. Misdaeus — last of the adversaries — is converted by the dust of the man he killed. The relics go West (to Edessa, in tradition). The churches hold. The book closes with a doxology. Everything that was separated at the beginning — Thomas from his Lord, the soul from its home, India from the gospel — is gathered back together at the end.*
